author: Agence France Presse
description:
• Barcelona 7-0 Real Madrid

  • Lead at the top stretched to five points

Clàudia Pina smashed in four goals as Barcelona demolished Real Madrid 7-0 to earn a five point lead at the top of Liga F on Sunday over their rivals.

The 25-year-old Spain international was in lethal form in front of goal as a dominant Barça won the Clásico battle with ease at the Camp Nou in front of over 40,000 fans, continuing their perfect start to the campaign. The match was pushed back by two hours after torrential rain in the Catalonia region over the weekend.

Continue reading...
title: Clàudia Pina hits four as Barcelona score seven goals to demolish Real Madrid

author: Agencies
description:
• Rams score two touchdowns in final four minutes

  • Kansas City Chiefs edge Las Vegas to stay unbeaten

  • Lamar Jackson leaves stadium in protective boot

  • Drake Maye finds form in Pats win over Bills

Kyren Williams ran for two touchdowns in the final four minutes as Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams rallied from a 10-point deficit to beat the Philadelphia Eagles. The Rams had struggled offensively all afternoon and a win seemed out of reach until late in the fourth quarter, when Eagles coach Nick Sirianni decided against kicking a chip-shot field goal that would have made it a three-score game and instead went for it on fourth down. The Eagles failed to convert, giving the Rams new life. Stafford led touchdown drives of 98 and 79 yards, with Williams scoring the go-ahead touchdown from seven yards out. Both teams are 2-2 on the season.
title: NFL roundup: Rams escape against Eagles, Chiefs win thriller but Thornton suffers gruesome injury

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
Reform UK leader was interviewed for half an hour last month over money from crypto billionaire

Nigel Farage has been interviewed by the standards commissioner for an investigation into whether he should have declared a £5m gift from the crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne.

The Reform UK leader spent about half an hour being questioned over the money, the Sunday Times reported. Farage maintains the gift was for his personal security.

title: Nigel Farage questioned by standards commissioner over £5m gift

author: Carmen Aguilar García, Sally Weale and Johnny McDevitt
description:
Exclusive: Average of nearly five sexual crimes a day against under-13s were reported to police between 2021 and 2025

  • From unwanted touching to rape: the scale of child-on-child abuse in English and Welsh schools

Lawyers and campaigners have condemned the “horrifying” scale of child-on-child sexual abuse in schools after a Guardian investigation revealed thousands of sexual offences against under-13s, including multiple rapes, are reported to police every year.

Close to five sexual crimes against children aged 12 and younger were recorded on average by police every day in primary and secondary schools in England and Wales, according to Guardian analysis of police data for 2021-25.

Continue reading...
title: Thousands of child-on-child sexual offences reported at schools in England and Wales

author: Agencies
description:
• Ty France’s ninth-inning drive hits roof cable

  • Brewers go on to win NLDS opener 3-2

Brewers manager Pat Murphy credited the team’s legendary late broadcaster Bob Uecker for an unlikely boost in the ninth inning to help preserve a 3-2 victory over visiting San Diego in ⁠the opener of their playoff series on Saturday.

With one out in the ninth and the Brewers clinging to a one-run lead, San Diego had a runner on first when Ty France hit a drive to left field ⁠off closer Trevor Megill. But the ball struck a roof cable, stayed in play and was caught by Jackson Chourio for the second out. Megill then retired Jackson Merrill on a fly ball to right field to ⁠give Milwaukee the victory.

Continue reading...
title: Cable robs Padres of potential home run in bizarre playoff loss to Brewers

author: Giles Richards
description:
• First win of season for Dutchman after long rain delay

  • Heartbreak for Russell as power units struggle in weather

Max Verstappen won a chaotic Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia with a dominant drive for Red Bull, his and the team’s first win of the season beating the Mercedes of Kimi Antonelli into second. With the Italian’s teammate and title rival George Russell forced to retire with five laps to go it has left the British driver’s title hopes shattered and Antonelli within touching distance of the championship.

Lewis Hamilton was third for Ferrari making a remarkable comeback after a torrid afternoon, starting on the slick rubber in the wet which dropped him as far back as 17th before coming back with a superb drive, including a late pass on Isack Hadjar who finished fifth. Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc was fourth after a race marked by farcical scenes before it was even underway as this season’s engine formula was found sorely wanting the fi
title: Max Verstappen wins chaotic F1 Bahrain GP in Malaysia after rain causes farcical scenes

author: Angus Fontaine at Accor Stadium
description:
• Roosters claim 16th title with 19-18 win in Sydney

  • Mark Nawaqanitawase scores twice after Newcastle held 12-0 lead

After a Cinderella season that took them from wooden spooners to a grand final, Newcastle went within a whisker of one of the greatest upsets in rugby league history, falling 19-18 to a dominant Sydney Roosters in the NRL decider in Sydney. Outclassed all day but never outgunned, the Knights scored with minutes to play to set up a thrilling finish, only for the men from Bondi to deny them at the death.

Led by their inspirational captain, James Tedesco – a worthy Clive Churchill winner – the Roosters squeezed the life out of Newcastle’s rags to riches story, farewelling their rugby union-bound stars Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase in style, the dynamic winger crossing for two spectacular tries as the Roosters’ kicking game nailed the Newcastle underdogs in their own half and didn’t let them out.
title: Sydney Roosters hold off brave Newcastle Knights to win thrilling NRL grand final

author: Jeff Rueter at State Farm Stadium
description:
• Sullivan becomes youngest-ever scorer in USMNT history

  • Julian Hall and Mailk Tillman also score

The last time the United States and Mexico played at this building, Jimmy Conrad and Landon Donovan provided the goals in one of several 2-0 wins for the US. On Saturday, the US squad included eight players who hadn’t yet been born when that happened.

The young United States went one better from their forebears, though, silencing a sizable pro-Mexico contingent in a composed 3-0 triumph that fully announced the arrival of an exciting new generation of players. Cavan Sullivan, just a few days after turning 17, became the youngest goal scorer in the history of the program with an eye-catching long-range chip. Julian Hall, 18, scored his third goal in as many games. Malik Tillman capped the scoring in the 85th minute, humbling a ten-man Mexico after they’d opened the match with far more strength.

The US haven’t played an away game since
title: Cavan Sullivan’s long-range chip highlights USMNT’s 3-0 romp over Mexico
